goal: Ship the human-authored Suppression ledger paths — admin manual entry, owner do-not-contact, owner clearing of their own account rows, and the admin-only audited Correction path — plus the server-side §7.4 read helper and copy constants #629 renders.
non_goals: No recipient-facing surfaces — the /u/<token> landing path and Unsubscribe redemption shipped in #644
No rendering of §7.4 on the Requests surface — spec §11 hands that to #629; this ticket exports the read helper and copy constants it consumes
No re-subscribe control in any surface, for anyone, ever (§8.1)
No expiry, TTL, or reaper on a suppression row
No bulk owner import of a do-not-contact list (FU-5)
No automated parsing of reply-based or mailto opt-outs (FU-1) — §7.2 is a daily human check
No owner-visible suppression reason detail — bounce vs complaint vs unsubscribe stays server-side (FU-3)
No mailbox-liveness poller — §7.2 liveness is a documented probe
No job_outbox row on any suppression write (§9.3 — there is no follow-up work)
No new environment variable or feature flag (§10)
user_visible_behavior: An admin on /admin/suppressions can look up a raw email address and see every Suppression ledger row for that Normalized handle, with its Suppression scope, source, and when it was recorded
An admin can enter a manual opt-out: raw address + a required note carrying the originating message reference, writing scope='global', source='admin_manual', created_by_user_id
An address that fails normalizeEmail is rejected with a visible error rather than minting a wrong handle
Re-entering an address that is already globally suppressed reports 'already suppressed' and writes no second row

An admin can remove a factually-wrong suppression row through the Correction path, which requires a free-text reason and writes a correction record naming who removed it and why in the same transaction as the delete
The Correction path is labelled as error correction and never as re-subscribe, and appears in no owner-facing or recipient-facing surface
An owner on /dashboard/requests/contacts can mark a contact do-not-contact, writing scope='account', source='owner_manual', their account_id and created_by_user_id
An owner can clear a do-not-contact they created; the control is absent for a contact suppressed by a global row
A suppressed contact is shown to the owner as opted out of RepWorth review requests, never as merely skipped
An owner's own do-not-contact is visually distinguishable from a global opt-out, because only the former is reversible by them
invariants: Invariant #8 tenant isolation — every owner read/write is scoped by account_id; a global row's account_id provenance is never surfaced to any owner, on any surface
Invariant #14 posture — solicitation_suppressions stays server-owned with RLS deny-all; no browser code reads or writes it
Invariant #15 — domain modules take their Sql/TransactionSql client as an explicit parameter; only route handlers import the singleton
§8.1 — no re-subscribe, no expiry, and attestation never overrides suppression
§7.6 — an owner may never clear a global row, and the UI must not present the two controls as the same thing
G7 — suppressionMatchSql stays the single owner of the §1.2 lookup predicate; no call site re-implements it and no isSuppressed() wrapper is introduced
G3 — global wins a double match, in the lookup and in the display state
G11 — the source/scope pairing stays one-directional and DB-enforced; owner_manual is the only account-scoped source
§2.1 first-write-wins — a manual entry never overwrites an existing row
DR1 — no suppression-path code reads SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED
DR2 — the ledger stays solicitation-only; no transactional or notification path consults it
§9.4/§9.5 — the Normalized handle never reaches an analytics property or a log message
The Correction path is admin-only, AAL2-gated, and reachable from no owner or recipient entry point
edge_cases: A global admin_manual row has account_id = NULL by construction — a mailbox reply carries no account — so the correction record must not require one; this is why account_audit_log (account_id NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts) cannot be the sink
A provider_suppressed mirror originating on the transactional side (§3.3) is the second account_id-NULL case the Correction path must handle
An admin entry for a handle already suppressed globally is a no-op success, not an error and not a second row
An admin entry for a handle that only has an account-scoped row still writes the global row — different partial unique index, both rows coexist
An owner marking do-not-contact on a contact with no email is refused — there is no handle to key on
An owner clearing a handle that is suppressed both globally and by their own account row removes only their account row; the contact stays suppressed and the surface keeps saying so
An owner attempting to clear a global row is refused, and the control is not rendered in the first place
A contact id belonging to another account returns the same uniform 404 as a non-existent one
A correction on a row that another admin already removed reports not-found rather than writing an orphan correction record
The correction record must survive the account whose id it carries as provenance — no FK to accounts, or a purge would CASCADE away a compliance record

The §7.4 read helper must distinguish global from account without re-deriving the predicate — suppressionMatchSql gains scope in its projection rather than the caller inferring it from source = 'owner_manual'
Contacts store the already-normalized email, so no owner-side path re-normalizes; the admin path is the only one that calls normalizeEmail, because it alone takes raw input

estimated_prod_lines: ±750 production+migration lines (migration 098 ~70; suppression.ts read helper + copy + scope projection ~90; admin suppressions service ~105; admin routes ~150; admin page + client ~230; owner suppression route ~100; contacts-repo + ContactList ~60; nav-config + tenant-scope allowlist + docs ~45)
estimated_test_lines: ±1600 test lines — a compliance-record feature runs well above 1:1: two live-DB integration suites (correction atomicity, owner clear vs global row), four route suites under the AAL2 and tenant-scope gates, the §7.4 display-mapping unit + fast-check invariant, and two component suites
rollback_plan: Migration 098 is purely additive — one new table, no FK to accounts, no change to any existing table or index — so nothing in the ledger, the batch build, or the purge depends on it. To back out: revert the app deploy FIRST (the admin routes are the only writers), then DROP TABLE solicitation_suppression_corrections, which is safe while empty and loses only correction history when not. No flag flip is involved: the admin paths are deliberately unflagged, and the owner paths ride the existing SOLICITATION_WATCH_ENABLED gate, so turning that off removes the owner surface without touching any row. Migrations apply staging-first, then prod in lockstep at promotion.
observability: A row in solicitation_suppression_corrections is the durable proof a Correction path removal happened: it names the suppression id, scope, source, the removing admin, and the reason — query it to answer 'who removed this and why'

The existing solicitation_suppressed analytics event fires on every manual write with source/scope/channel properties (never the handle), so admin_manual and owner_manual volumes are countable alongside the machine sources
Structured log lines on the admin routes carry the suppression row id and never the Normalized handle (§9.5), so a correction is traceable in Railway logs without leaking a recipient address

A §7.2 servicing failure is invisible in code by design — the mailbox liveness probe documented in the channels runbook is what proves opt-outs are still arriving; a zero-admin_manual month with a live forward is the signal to check it
